title: MBARI DeepSea-MOT
vessel: MBARI ROVs Doc Ricketts and Ventana
notes: A multi-object-tracking benchmark for deep-sea video. B* sequences are benthic and M* midwater, which matters: a midwater detector scores nothing on the benthic ones. Recorded at 1920x1080 and 25 to 60 frames a second - a different camera from the 640x360 proxies every NOAA cruise here is read at, which is the standing caveat on every number scored against it.

title: Hohonu Moana: Exploring Deep Waters off Hawaii
vessel: NOAA Ship Okeanos Explorer, ROV Deep Discoverer
notes: Hawaii and Johnston Atoll, to 2484 m. The same waters as EX2503 a decade earlier, which is the other pair in this catalogue that can be compared across time.

title: Deepwater Exploration of the Marianas
vessel: NOAA Ship Okeanos Explorer, ROV Deep Discoverer
notes: Mariana Trench Marine National Monument; hydrothermal and seamount sites. Nineteen dives, and dive 3 worked at 4996 m - the deepest footage in this catalogue, which is not something the collection knew until its dive reports could be read.

title: Deepwater Wonders of Wake
vessel: NOAA Ship Okeanos Explorer, ROV Deep Discoverer
notes: Wake Atoll and the seamounts of the western Pacific, to 2250 m.

title: Mountains in the Deep: Exploring the Central Pacific Basin
vessel: NOAA Ship Okeanos Explorer, ROV Deep Discoverer
notes: Seamounts around American Samoa and the Central Pacific Basin.

title: Océano Profundo 2018: Exploring Deep-sea Habitats off Puerto Rico
vessel: NOAA Ship Okeanos Explorer, ROV Deep Discoverer
notes: The Puerto Rico trench and the island's deep slopes - the only Caribbean footage here, and the only place in the catalogue where the Atlantic reaches 8,000 m.

title: Windows to the Deep 2019
vessel: NOAA Ship Okeanos Explorer, ROV Deep Discoverer
notes: 19 dives on the Blake Plateau and Blake Escarpment, the deepest at 3498 m. The earlier half of the only repeat visit in this catalogue - see EX2107.

title: Windows to the Deep 2021
vessel: NOAA Ship Okeanos Explorer, ROV Deep Discoverer
notes: Deep-sea coral and sponge habitats off the US southeast; 14 dives, the deepest at 3650 m. Pairs with EX1903L2, which worked the same mounds two years earlier: the only two cruises here that visited the same place twice.

title: Voyage to the Ridge 2
vessel: NOAA Ship Okeanos Explorer, ROV Deep Discoverer
notes: The Mid-Atlantic Ridge and the Azores Plateau, mid-ocean rift valley and fracture zones, to 3350 m. The only Atlantic-ridge footage in the catalogue.

title: Voyage to the Ridge 3
vessel: NOAA Ship Okeanos Explorer, ROV Deep Discoverer
notes: The northern Mid-Atlantic Ridge and the Azores, three weeks after EX2205 worked the same ridge further south.

title: EXPRESS 2023 - West Coast Exploration
vessel: NOAA Ship Okeanos Explorer, ROV Deep Discoverer
notes: California and Oregon margin, submarine canyons and seamounts to 3956 m.

title: Seascape Alaska 5
vessel: NOAA Ship Okeanos Explorer, ROV Deep Discoverer
notes: Gulf of Alaska seamounts and continental slope, 55-59 degrees north. Nineteen dives, the deepest at 4262 m. Cold, high-latitude deep sea - a different fauna from everything else here.

title: Beyond the Blue: Papahanaumokuakea 2025
vessel: NOAA Ship Okeanos Explorer, ROV Deep Discoverer
notes: Seamounts and abyssal plain in and around Papahanaumokuakea, Central Pacific. Dive 2 worked at 4859 m and dive 13 at 4599 m, out near the dateline - the deepest of the four cruises in this section, and second only to EX1605L1.

title: Gulf of Alaska Seamount Expedition 2004
notes: Alvin dives on the Gulf of Alaska seamounts, nineteen years before EX2306 worked the same water with an ROV. Footage from a human-occupied submersible, which is a different way of looking: a pilot turning to what a scientist in the sphere asked to see. No clock and no navigation are published with it.

title: Hidden Ocean 2005: Arctic Exploration
notes: Under the Arctic ice in the Canada Basin - the only polar footage in this catalogue, and the only footage taken from an icebreaker. No clock and no navigation are published with it.

title: Monterey Bay National Marine Sanctuary 2000
notes: Monterey Canyon in 2000 - the same water MBARI's annotated sequences come from, twenty-three years earlier and through a different camera. No clock and no navigation are published with it.

title: Axial Seamount ASHES vent field, 2016-2026
archive: Ocean Observatories Initiative Regional Cabled Array
vessel: Fixed camera CAMHDA301, cabled to shore
notes: A high-definition camera in the ASHES hydrothermal vent field on Axial Seamount, 1542 m deep on the Juan de Fuca Ridge. It runs a scripted pan and zoom over the sulphide chimneys and their tubeworm cover every three hours. Five recordings a decade apart, same day of year, same hour.
